document: Zerodha Varsity Decay Research vs OptionPilot Pro Dashboard — Concept Comparison
method: Every 'dashboard_status' entry below was verified by reading server.ts directly (grep + line inspection), not recalled from memory. Every 'varsity_teaches' entry is paraphrased from Zerodha Varsity Module 5 (Theta, Moneyness, Vega chapters) — not copied verbatim, per copyright limits.

comparison.varsity_teaches: Premium = Intrinsic Value + Time Value. These are the only two components of any option's price.
comparison.dashboard_status: NOT COMPUTED. PremiumData stores the raw premium (lastPrice) but never splits it into intrinsic vs. time value.
comparison.implication: The dashboard currently cannot tell the user how much of a 700–900 premium is 'real' (intrinsic) vs. 'decaying' (time value) — the exact gap that started this whole conversation.

comparison.varsity_teaches: CE intrinsic = Spot − Strike (floored at 0). PE intrinsic = Strike − Spot (floored at 0). Never negative.
comparison.dashboard_status: NOT COMPUTED anywhere in the codebase. Spot and strike are both already available on every PremiumData record, so this is trivial to add.
comparison.implication: Single highest-value, lowest-risk addition identified across both research passes.

comparison.varsity_teaches: Any strike with intrinsic value > 0 is ITM; zero intrinsic value is OTM; strike ≈ spot is ATM. For calls, ITM strikes are below ATM; for puts, ITM strikes are above ATM.
comparison.dashboard_status: PARTIAL. Only isAtm: boolean exists on PremiumData. No isItm/isOtm flag or classification function exists — would need to be derived ad hoc from spot vs. strike at read time.
comparison.implication: The dashboard can already tell you what's ATM, but not systematically what's ITM/OTM or how deep.

comparison.varsity_teaches: Theta is the ₹ (or points) an option loses per day, all else equal. It's a real, computable per-day rate.
comparison.dashboard_status: PRESENT. calcGreeks() computes full Black-Scholes theta per ATM CE/PE leg, displayed in the Premium Pair card ('Vega / Theta' row).
comparison.implication: This part of the Varsity framework was already built — no gap here, contrary to this session's earlier assumption (from an outdated 2026-07-25 decision) that Greeks were skipped entirely.

comparison.concept: Decay curve shape (non-linear, accelerates near expiry)
comparison.varsity_teaches: Decay is flat with many days left and accelerates sharply in the final stretch — Varsity's own worked example: 20 points lost over 20 days at 120→100 DTE, a small early-series move.
comparison.dashboard_status: NOT SURFACED. The underlying Black-Scholes formula mathematically implies this (theta grows as time-to-expiry shrinks), but theta is read fresh each cycle as an instantaneous snapshot — nothing compares it to its own recent history or flags 'decay is accelerating.'
comparison.match: IMPLIED BY MATH, NOT SURFACED AS A FEATURE
comparison.implication: A genuine decay-acceleration alert would need history tracking that doesn't exist yet — flagged in the earlier examination report as a recommended future step, gated on enough history to avoid false alarms (same principle as the Outcome Engine's MIN_SAMPLE_SIZE).

comparison.varsity_teaches: Vega measures premium change per 1-point IV move, independent of spot. Around known events, IV rises beforehand and often crushes afterward — this alone can move a premium sharply even with a correct directional call.
comparison.dashboard_status: PRESENT for vega itself (calcGreeks() computes it per leg, displayed alongside theta). IV crush as a NAMED, TRACKED EVENT is NOT present — nothing flags 'IV just dropped sharply' as distinct from a normal theta-driven move.
comparison.match: PARTIAL — raw ingredient present, event-detection missing
comparison.implication: A user watching a premium fall could currently not tell, from the dashboard alone, whether it was theta, an IV crush, or the underlying moving against them — all three look the same on a raw price line.

comparison.concept: Delta/Gamma affect intrinsic; Theta/Vega affect extrinsic
comparison.varsity_teaches: This exact split was confirmed directly by Varsity's own author: Delta and Gamma move the intrinsic portion (they respond to spot); Theta and Vega move the extrinsic/time portion.
comparison.dashboard_status: All four Greeks (delta, vega, theta — gamma is NOT separately computed) exist as numbers, but nothing in the code groups them this way or uses the grouping to decompose a premium change.
comparison.implication: This is exactly the three-way decomposition (intrinsic Δ, theta Δ, vega/IV Δ) recommended in the research note — achievable by combining existing numbers, no new data source needed. Note gamma itself isn't currently computed (only vega/theta/delta), though it isn't required for this specific decomposition.

comparison.varsity_teaches: Indian index options are European — a buyer can only square off before expiry or let the contract settle at expiry, never exercise early.
comparison.dashboard_status: Correctly assumed throughout — no early-exercise logic exists anywhere, consistent with this fact.

comparison.varsity_teaches: Varsity's own worked examples use plain calendar-day counts divided by 365 for the T term — no special trading-day adjustment shown in the core theory chapters.
comparison.dashboard_status: daysToExpiry = (expiryDate − now) / 86,400,000ms — calendar-day only, matching Varsity's own textbook convention.
comparison.match: MATCH (textbook-consistent), THOUGH TRADING-DAY AWARENESS REMAINS A VALID REFINEMENT
comparison.implication: The earlier examination report's Step 1 (real holiday list → trading-day count) is not 'fixing an error' — it would be a refinement beyond what Varsity's own basic theory chapters model, useful but not urgent on textbook-correctness grounds alone.

comparison.concept: Buyer's condition for profit at expiry
comparison.varsity_teaches: An option must expire ITM for the buyer to have gained anything — confirmed directly by Varsity's author correcting a reader who suggested ATM/OTM could work.
comparison.dashboard_status: No feature currently states or reinforces this to the user — the dashboard shows current moneyness-adjacent data (isAtm) but doesn't frame 'buyer needs ITM at expiry' as an explicit takeaway anywhere.
comparison.match: MISSING AS AN EXPLICIT DASHBOARD MESSAGE
comparison.implication: Once isItm/isOtm exists (see row 3), a simple derived message becomes possible: e.g. 'this contract is currently OTM — needs spot to move X points to reach breakeven by expiry,' directly grounded in Varsity's own framing.

single_highest_priority_gap: Intrinsic/Extrinsic value split (rows 1 and 2) — zero new data required, directly closes the exact confusion (700–900 premium meaning different things depending on ITM vs ATM) that prompted this entire research thread.
